description: DA3408 A4: CPU-only BLIP captioning (Streamlit) with Prometheus app metrics and node_exporter.

options.content: **Live health, load, latency, errors and machine cost of the CPU-only BLIP image-captioning app.** Read top to bottom: *is it up?* → *how much work?* → *how fast?* → *what failed?* → *what was sent, by whom?* → *what did it cost the machine?* **Key (Okabe-Ito, colour-blind safe):** ■ single-image mode = solid line · ■ bulk ZIP mode = dashed line · **orange shaded bands = a bulk job is running** (shown on every chart, to line app spikes up with CPU/RAM). **Purple bands = an alert is firing.** X-axes are wall-clock time; every axis title gives the unit and the scale (all linear). **(range)** = total or mean over the selected time range. Hover one chart to see the same moment on all charts.

panels.title: 1 · Health: is the service up and ready?

options.content: Green UP / READY means Prometheus can scrape the app and node_exporter and the model is loaded. The timeline shows any outage; the alert tiles show what rules.yml is firing right now.

panels.description: Application health. UP when Prometheus scraped the target in the last second, DOWN when the scrape failed.
panels.title: App status

panels.description: Infrastructure health. UP when Prometheus scraped the target in the last second, DOWN when the scrape failed.
panels.title: Node exporter

panels.description: READY once the captioning model is loaded in memory and can serve requests.
panels.title: Model

panels.description: How long the caption app process has been running. A reset means a restart.
panels.title: App uptime

panels.description: Browser sessions currently connected to the Streamlit app.
panels.title: Open sessions

panels.description: Caption requests being processed right now (single + bulk).
panels.title: In flight now

panels.description: Images successfully captioned in the selected time range (single + bulk).
panels.title: Images (range)

panels.description: Failed attempts (corrupt images, bad ZIPs, model errors) as a share of all attempts in the selected range. Green below 5 %, orange 5-20 %, vermillion above 20 %.
panels.title: Failures (range)

panels.description: Each row is a scrape target; a DOWN block marks when Prometheus could not reach it. Text labels (UP/DOWN) carry the meaning, colour only reinforces it.
panels.title: Availability history · scrape status of every target
Alerts firing
panels.description: Number of alerts from rules.yml firing right now (Prometheus ALERTS series). NONE when all is well.

panels.title: Firing alerts · name, severity and target
panels.description: Alerts from rules.yml that are firing right now, most severe first. Empty when nothing is firing. Alertmanager forwards the same alerts to the webhook.

panels.title: 2 · Throughput: how much work is the app doing?

options.content: Bulk uploads show up as long orange plateaus of images/s and a queue of pending images; single uploads are short blue blips. Rates are averaged over the last 30 s.

panels.description: Successfully captioned images per second, split by mode (30 s rate). Bulk jobs dominate throughput.
panels.title: Throughput · images captioned per second

panels.description: Caption requests (one per button click) per minute, split by mode. A bulk request carries many images.
panels.title: Requests · uploads per minute

panels.description: Gauges: requests being processed now (per mode) and images still waiting inside running bulk jobs. A falling purple staircase is a bulk job draining.
panels.title: Work in progress · in-flight requests and queued bulk images
3 · Latency: how fast is each image captioned?

options.content: Per-image model time is ~1-2 s on this CPU. The step line moves as each image finishes and holds its value in between; the bars and tiles summarise every image in the selected time range.

panels.description: Model generate() time of the most recent image in each mode (gauge caption_last_inference_seconds). During a bulk job the orange step line moves once per image; it holds its value until the next image.
panels.title: Inference time per image · updates as each image finishes

panels.description: How many images (both modes) took each amount of model time over the selected range, from the caption_inference_seconds histogram buckets. Readable with a handful of images and with thousands.
panels.title: Latency distribution · images per inference-time bucket (range)

panels.description: Mean wall time of one request over the selected range, from the caption_request_seconds summary (_sum / _count): one image for single mode, the whole ZIP for bulk.
panels.title: Request time · mean per request (range)

panels.description: Mean time spent resizing and normalising an image before the model runs, over the selected range (caption_preprocess_seconds summary). A rise points at very large input images.
panels.title: Pre-processing · mean per image (range)

options.content: Bad inputs are expected in bulk ZIPs and are skipped without crashing the app; inference_error would point at the model itself.

panels.description: Errors counted per minute: invalid_image (corrupt/unreadable picture), bad_zip (upload is not a ZIP), inference_error (the model failed). Solid, dashed and dotted lines keep types apart without colour.
panels.title: Errors · per minute by type

panels.description: Failed attempts (corrupt images, bad ZIPs, model errors) as a share of all attempts since the app started. It steps at every failure and drifts down as good images are captioned; it has no gaps when the app is idle.
panels.title: Failure share · cumulative since app start

panels.description: Files inside uploaded ZIPs that were not captioned, by reason, over the selected range. Bar length and the number both show the count.
panels.title: Skipped ZIP entries · by reason (range)
5 · Inputs & clients: what was sent, and by whom?

options.content: Client labels (IP, Streamlit session, browser) come from each request; localhost is the IP Streamlit reports for local connections.

panels.description: Requests per client in the selected range, from the client_ip, session_id and browser labels on caption_requests_total. Sorted by most requests.
panels.title: Clients · requests per IP, session, browser and mode (range)

panels.description: Successfully captioned images per client IP over the selected range, one bar per mode (caption_images_processed_total with the client_ip label).
panels.title: Images captioned · per client IP, by mode (range)

panels.description: How large the uploaded images were (width × height in megapixels), from the caption_image_pixels histogram over the selected range. Big images cost more pre-processing.
panels.title: Input resolution · images per size bucket (range)

panels.description: Mean size of the uploaded file over the selected range (caption_upload_bytes summary): one image for single mode, the whole ZIP for bulk.
panels.title: Upload size · mean per request (range)

panels.description: Average number of images queued per uploaded ZIP over the selected range (histogram _sum / _count). The app caps a ZIP at 50 images.
panels.title: Bulk batch size · mean images per ZIP (range)

panels.description: Mean number of words per generated caption over the selected range (caption_length_words summary). A sudden drop would hint at degenerate model output.
panels.title: Caption length · mean words (range)

panels.description: Number of ZIP uploads that were processed over the selected range (caption_bulk_batch_images_count).
panels.title: Bulk jobs · ZIPs processed (range)
6 · System resources (node_exporter): what does the work cost the machine?

options.content: Corroboration: inside the orange bulk bands the machine CPU, the app's own CPU and bulk images/s (right axis) rise and fall together. Machine RAM stays roughly flat because the model is loaded once; the app's own memory grows a little during bulk jobs.

panels.description: Left axis: whole-machine CPU busy % (node_exporter, all cores) and the caption app's own share (process_cpu_seconds_total). Right axis: bulk images captioned per second. The three rise and fall together during bulk jobs.
panels.title: CPU vs workload · machine CPU, app CPU and bulk throughput

panels.description: Left axis: machine RAM in use % (MemAvailable based). Right axis: resident memory of the caption app process, mostly the ~0.9 GB BLIP model.
panels.title: Memory · machine RAM used and caption app resident memory

panels.description: Runnable processes averaged over 1 min. Above the dashed line (number of cores) work is queueing for CPU.
panels.title: Load average · 1 min load vs CPU cores

panels.description: Bytes per second read from and written to physical disks (30 s rate). Model loading shows up as reads.
panels.title: Disk I/O · read and write throughput

panels.description: Share of the root filesystem in use. Green below 85 %, orange 85-95 %, vermillion above 95 %.
panels.title: Root disk · used on /

panels.description: Memory taken by the model weights (caption_model_size_bytes).
panels.title: Model weights · memory

panels.description: Seconds the app took to load the model (caption_model_load_seconds).
panels.title: Model load time · at startup

panels.description: Current resident memory of the caption app process.
panels.title: App memory · resident
